narrative: Your law school application was denied because the model estimated an 84% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a high-risk estimate, not a certainty, but it was strong enough to drive the admission decision. The most influential factor was your very low third-year class standing: you were in the first decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. This was the strongest push toward a “fail” prediction. Your first-year class standing was the second most influential factor; at the second decile, also well below the accepted-student average near the sixth decile, it added further risk. Your LSAT score was the third most important factor: a 30 compared with an accepted-student average of about 37 pushed the prediction toward failure as well. Other information, such as your undergraduate GPA being close to the accepted average, did not outweigh these signals. To move forward, ask admissions for feedback, meet with an academic advisor, and consider whether retaking the LSAT or completing additional coursework could strengthen a future application. If immediate admission is not possible, discuss alternative programs or a reapplication plan with clear evidence of improved readiness.
